speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, such as whether it is flat, raised, or blister-like? Also, when did the rash first appear relative to the onset of your fever and cold symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash on the trunk have a "slapped cheek" appearance on the face, and does the body rash look like a lacy or net-like pattern? Are there any joint pains or swelling in her hands or knees?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the characteristic facial rash sparing the perioral area and the subsequent lacy body rash, the clinical presentation is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Fifth Disease (Parvovirus B19 infection)
